items.title: Warfare 2026, Farnborough UK, 14-15 November
items.summary: Attendees compare impressions of the Farnborough show over the weekend, including a quieter Sunday and reports from vendors about Saturday’s trade.

items.summary: A post on tabletop scenarios or rules from Wargaming Miscellany. Filed under Book Review. Topics include scenario design.

items.title: The Adventures of Kampfgruppe Klink
items.summary: A reader asks what happened to the lead German motorcycle squad in a Soviet ambush. The reply fills in a missing detail from the battle report as the squad moves through a village toward the bridge.

items.title: 20mm Spanish Civil War Crossfire
items.summary: A Pendraken member shares a Spanish Civil War game played with 20mm figures and Crossfire rules. The thread links to the full battle report on Mad Lemmey’s blog.

items.title: Warflag - Free flags site
items.summary: Readers trade tips on finding printable miniature flags. One reply points to archived NapFlags pages in the Wayback Machine for material from the old site.

items.title: Roman Marching Camp in 10mm and 28mm!
items.summary: A community thread on a Roman marching camp offered in two scales. It is a lead for anyone looking for a fortified camp to go with either a 10mm or 28mm ancient army.

items.title: Nineteen million hits!
items.summary: Bob Cordery marks 19 million recorded visits to Wargaming Miscellany. He also wonders how much of the recent traffic comes from automated visitors, a question that puts the site’s next readership milestone in perspective.

items.title: Remote wargame - Second Battle of Azukizaka, 1548
items.summary: Peter refights Azukizaka over a remote tabletop using Daniel Mersey’s Arrowstorm. His Sengoku house rules bind arquebusiers, ashigaru and samurai into a single formation, giving the medieval rules a distinct feel for this matchup.

items.title: Got this from the Library. 1977. Lovely old school.
items.summary: A hobby journal entry covering 18th Century from Flintlock & Tomahawk. Filed under American Revolution.

items.title: Stalled ... and I'm not sure how to get my project restarted
items.summary: After writing Portable Wargame rules and creating twelve fictional nations, Bob Cordery has stalled on his Belle Époque project. He takes inventory of the work already done, including flags and army backstories, as he thinks through how to resume.

items.title: Friday Night at the Fights
items.summary: Jonathan Freitag puts his 28mm Punic Wars collection on the table to introduce Austin to Basic Impetvs. It follows a run of Commands & Colors: Ancients games and offers a look at the same period through another ruleset.

items.title: Scenarios for Wargames: Forty-five years late!
items.summary: Bob Cordery finally picks up Charles Stewart Grant’s 1981 scenario book through a secondhand listing. Its 52 tabletop situations are the draw, and he plans to try some of them in the coming months.

items.title: New YouTube video: The Portable Wargame in action: The hunt for the Mahdi
items.summary: This 17-minute video revisits a solo battle from the original Portable Wargame book. The action takes place on a square grid and uses an early version of the rules later developed for The Portable Colonial Wargame.

items.title: Wrapping up the Anglo-Zulu project
items.summary: The British and Zulu armies are ready for their first game. The final painting batch adds Natal Native Contingent infantry and horse, British command stands, camp tents and a rocket launcher built from wire and plastic.

items.title: The next Portable Wargame Compendium: Another progress report
items.summary: The next compendium is taking shape around Belle Époque rules, solo club campaigns and a fast-play Peninsular War system. The lineup also includes a boxed 1814–15 campaign and a comparison with the Coffeebreak rules.

items.title: Picardie Regiment and Teaching Rules
items.summary: The French Picardie Regiment joins Jonathan Freitag’s growing War of the Spanish Succession collection. The photos show Ebor Miniatures infantry with flags from Not By Appointment, a useful pairing for anyone building a French line.

items.title: Nugget 385
items.summary: Issue 385 of Wargame Developments’ newsletter has come back from the printer and is heading to members. It is the third issue of the 2026–27 subscription year, and Bob Cordery also plans to send a PDF to the group’s webmaster.

items.title: HMS Dreadnought
items.summary: This naval history note follows Edward Reed’s earlier ironclad HMS Dreadnought through Mediterranean service, a Chatham refit and coastguard duty at Bantry Bay.

items.title: The eleventh hour of the eleventh day of the eleventh month
items.summary: Bob Cordery records two local acts of remembrance, including a Shrewsbury House performance that used readings and poetry to bring out the voices of people who lived through the First World War.

items.title: Another British ironclads in 1/1200th-scale
items.summary: A secondhand model of HMS Dreadnought brings Bob Cordery’s 1:1200 ironclad collection to nine vessels. The post is a quick look at the latest addition to a growing late-Victorian naval collection.

items.title: Last Stand at Salem Church
items.summary: Jonathan Freitag closes a six-game series of Salem Church refights with his account of the October 27 remote game. The companion report at Grid Based Wargaming gives the Union player’s view of the same fight.

items.title: Anglo-Zulu War camp and more units painted
items.summary: Peter builds a Zulu camp from half-spheres textured to resemble thatch. Painted card walls curve around the huts on the table and store flat between games, a practical way to make an enclosure without adding bulk.

items.title: Remembrance Day
items.summary: A hobby journal entry from AJ’s Wargaming Table.

items.title: New YouTube video: Aggressor, Krasnovia, and OPFOR
items.summary: An 18-minute video looks at fictional opponents used by the US Army in training. It traces the idea from the Second World War through later opposing-force exercises.

items.title: The Last of the Mohicans; A narrative of 1757 by James Fenimore Cooper
items.summary: The blog revisits James Fenimore Cooper’s novel on its bicentenary and links to the Project Gutenberg edition. Its 1757 frontier setting makes it a period read for French and Indian War gamers.

items.title: Gardes Francaises
items.summary: The first French infantry regiment in this War of the Spanish Succession project uses 17 Ebor figures and flags from Not By Appointment. The project photos follow an earlier look at the Dutch troops, so both sides are taking shape.

items.title: Shedquarters Day Q4 2026 - Crossing the Ebro
items.summary: This corps-scale NQM playtest covers the first six days of the Republican offensive in July 1938. With up to 18 turns and enough troops to require a third Republican player, the report looks at both the table logistics and what the offensive was meant to achieve.
